Shanghai Tower. The 128-story supertall skyscraper completed in 2015 in Shanghai, China, rising 2,073 feet and currently the world's second-tallest building. Its spiraling form and advanced environmental systems represent the cutting edge of twenty-first-century sustainable high-rise design. Designed by the international firm Gensler, the tower's distinctive twisted silhouette reduces wind loading and creates a dynamic appearance as the building spirals toward the sky. At 632 meters tall, it is the tallest building in China and surpassed only by the Burj Khalifa worldwide, reflecting China's ascendant economic and architectural ambitions. The facade incorporates a double-skin envelope with photovoltaic panels and a rainwater collection system that supplies energy and water to building operations. The tower houses office space, luxury residences, a hotel, and a retail complex, with the observation deck spanning multiple floors and offering 360-degree views of Shanghai and the Yangtze River. It contains China's first hotel-occupancy observation deck, advanced fire suppression systems, and earthquake engineering tailored to the building's height and location. Completed during China's rapid urbanization, it represents the country's emergence as a global economic and technological power in the twenty-first century.
